CHAPTER TWO
REAL ESTATE REGULATORY AUTHORITY
3. Real Estate Regulatory Authority.—The Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish an Authority for such area as may be specified by the Government by notification under sub-section (1) of section 20 of the Act.
4. Selection of Chairperson and other Members of Authority.—(1) The State Government shall make a reference to the Selection Committee for the appointment of the Chairperson and Member of the Authority or when any post in the Authority is vacant or likely to become vacant, for filling any such vacant post.
(2) The Selection Committee may follow such procedure as it may deem fit for the purpose of selecting the Chairperson or Member of the Authority.
(3) For filling the vacant post or vacant posts directed by the State Government, the Selection Committee shall make a recommendation for consideration in the form of a panel of persons not exceeding three, in order of preference separately to the State Government.
(4) The Selection Committee shall make its recommendation to the State Government within a period not exceeding sixty days from the date of reference made under sub-rule (1).
(5) The Selection Committee shall normally hold its meeting at Mumbai or at such other place in the State as it may organize or as the Chairperson may decide at any place.
(6) The notice/agenda of the meeting of the Selection Committee as the case may be, shall be fixed by the convener of the committee in consultation with the Chairperson of the Selection Committee regarding the date and venue of the meeting.
(7) The Secretary of the Housing Department shall be the convener of the Selection Committee.
5. Appointment of Chairperson and Members.—The State Government shall consider the recommendation of the Selection Committee for the appointment of the Chairperson and Members or for filling the vacant post in order of preference as per the recommendation made by the Selection Committee. If the State Government does not appoint a person in order of preference, the State Government shall record the reasons therefor in writing.

CHAPTER THREE
SALARY AND ALLOWANCES
6. Salaries and allowances and other conditions of service of Chairperson and Members of Authority.—
(a) The Chairperson and Members of the Authority shall be paid salaries and allowances as follows:—
(one) The Chairperson of the Authority shall be paid a monthly salary equivalent to the monthly salary of the Chief Secretary of the State Government;
(two) The Members of the Authority shall be paid a salary equivalent to the salary of the Principal Secretary of the State Government;
(three) Dearness Allowance and City Compensatory Allowance.—The Chairperson and Member shall be entitled to receive dearness allowance and city compensatory allowance at such rates as are admissible to the Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary of the State Government respectively.
(b) Leave.—(one) The Chairperson and Member shall be entitled to thirty days of earned leave for every year of service. They shall be entitled to leave salary during the leave period as admissible to the Chief Secretary or Principal Secretary of the State Government, as the case may be. The Chairperson or Member shall be entitled to encashment of fifty percent of the earned leave standing to their credit at any time.

(b) In case of the Members of the Authority, the Chairperson shall be the leave sanctioning authority.
(c) Travelling allowance and daily allowance.—(one) The Chairperson and Member of the Authority while on tour (including the journey undertaken for travel or upon expiry of his term to proceed to his hometown) shall be entitled to receive travelling allowance, daily allowance, transportation of personal effects and other similar matters at the same rates as admissible to the Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary of the State Government respectively.
(two) The Chairperson shall be the controlling officer in respect of bills relating to travelling allowance and daily allowance.
(d) Domestic official tours.—The Chairperson and Members while on tour shall be entitled to the facility of government accommodation in guest houses or inspection bungalows run by the State Government or, if government accommodation is not available, to hotel accommodation as admissible to the Chief Secretary or Principal Secretary of the Government of Maharashtra, as the case may be.
(e) Leave Travel Concession.—The Chairperson and Members shall be entitled to Leave Travel Concession (L.T.C.) at the same rates as admissible to the Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary of the State Government respectively.
(f) Medical facilities.—The Chairperson and Members shall be entitled to medical treatment and hospital facilities as provided to the members of the Indian Administrative Service of the corresponding grade in the State Government.
(g) Official visits abroad.—The Chairperson and Members shall be entitled to undertake official visits abroad with the prior approval of the Minister-in-Charge of the Housing Department and after clearance from the Ministry of External Affairs on points related to political affairs, and the daily allowance and accommodation during the period of tour abroad shall be regulated in accordance with the orders of the State Government applicable to the Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary respectively.
(h) Conveyance facility.—The Chairperson and Members shall be entitled to conveyance facilities as admissible to the Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary of the State Government respectively.
(i) Accommodation for Chairperson and Members.—(one) The Chairperson of the Authority shall be entitled to such accommodation as is admissible to the Chief Secretary of the State Government.
(two) The Member shall be entitled to such accommodation as is admissible to the rank of Principal Secretary of the State Government drawing equivalent pay. Upon resigning from the post, the Chairperson and Members shall be entitled to retain such accommodation on the same terms and conditions for a period up to one month:
Provided that if the Chairperson or Member of the Authority is residing in his own accommodation, he shall be paid house rent allowance at the same rate as admissible to the Chief Secretary or Principal Secretary of the State Government respectively.
(j) Telephone facility.—The Chairperson and Members of the Authority shall be entitled to telephone facilities as admissible to the Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary of the State Government respectively.
(k) Other allowances.—The Chairperson and Members of the Authority shall be entitled to such other allowances as are applicable to the Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary of the State Government respectively.
7. If an officer in the service of the State Government or Central Government is appointed as the Chairperson or, as the case may be, Member of the Authority, he shall be entitled to salary and allowances as per rule 6 during the period he holds such post:
Provided that such entitlement shall not be less than the entitlement to which he would have been otherwise eligible as a serving government servant.
8. Tenure of office.—(1) The term of office of the Chairperson and Members shall be in accordance with sub-section (1) of section 23 of the Act.
(2) When the Chairperson is unable to discharge his duties due to death, resignation, absence, illness or any other cause, the seniormost Member of the Authority (in order of appointment) holding office for the time being shall discharge the duties of the Chairperson until the day the Chairperson resumes charge of his duties or until the vacant posts are filled in accordance with section 24 of the Act.

9. Oath of office and secrecy.—(1) Every person appointed as Chairperson of the Authority shall, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe an oath of office and secrecy before the Minister-in-Charge of the Housing Department of the Government in Form One and Form Two respectively appended to these rules.
(2) Every person appointed as Member of the Authority shall, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe an oath of office and secrecy before the Chairperson of the Authority in Form One and Form Two respectively appended to these rules.
10. Disclosure of financial or other interest.—Before appointment, the Chairperson and every Member shall submit a declaration in Form Three that he has not acquired and shall not acquire any financial or other interest of such nature as is likely to affect prejudicially his functioning as such Chairperson or Member.

CHAPTER FOUR
PROCEDURE FOR INQUIRY AND REMOVAL OF CHAIRPERSON AND MEMBERS
11. Procedure for inquiry.—(1) Whenever the State Government is of the opinion that there are reasonable grounds for holding an inquiry against the Chairperson or Member on the grounds specified in sub-section (1) of section 26 of the Act, the State Government may, after consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court at Bombay, appoint a Judge for the purpose of conducting such inquiry.
(2) The Government shall communicate to the Judge so appointed the details of the charges against the Chairperson or, as the case may be, the Member.
(3) The State Government shall forward to the Judge so appointed copies of,—
(a) the statement of charges against the Chairperson or, as the case may be, the Member;
(b) copies of important documents and other evidence connected with the inquiry.
12. Powers of the Judge.—(1) The Judge so appointed shall deliver or cause to be delivered to the Chairperson or, as the case may be, the Member a copy of the statement of charges and a list of documents, if any, and shall require him to submit a written reply or statement of his defense within such time as may be allowed.
(2) The Judge shall follow principles of natural justice and shall have power to regulate his own procedure, including fixing the place and time of the inquiry.
(3) While conducting an inquiry into any case, the Judge shall have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908) for discharging his duties under these rules, namely:—
(a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath;
(b) requiring the discovery and production of documents;
(c) receiving evidence on affidavits; and
(d) subject to the provisions of sections 123 and 124 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (1 of 1872), requiring any office to produce any public record or document or copy thereof.
(4) Where it is alleged that the Chairperson or Member is unable to perform the duties of his office due to any physical or mental incapacity and such allegation is denied, the Judge may take such necessary action as deemed fit for medical examination of the Chairperson or Member.
(5) After the conclusion of the inquiry, the Judge shall submit his report to the State Government stating separately his findings on each charge and the reasons therefor along with his observations. The findings and the inquiry report clearly indicating whether the allegations are proved or not shall be submitted to the State Government along with the inquiry report.
(6) Based on the inquiry report received with such recommendations, the State Government shall, after consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court at Bombay, take a decision by order regarding the removal or otherwise of the Chairperson or, as the case may be, the Member.

13. Filling of vacancy.—The State Government shall initiate necessary action under rule 4 to fill the vacancy of the Chairperson or, as the case may be, the Member caused by such removal.

CHAPTER V
SERVICE CONDITIONS OF OFFICERS AND OTHER EMPLOYEES OF THE AUTHORITY
14. Categories and pay scales of officers and employees of the Authority.—The Authority shall recommend to the State Government for consideration the names of officers and employees required in the office of the Authority, which may be approved by the State Government with or without modifications, as the case may be. Their appointments shall be made in accordance with the regulations of the Authority as approved by the State Government.
15. Conditions of service.—The conditions of service of the officers and employees of the Authority in respect of pay, allowances, leave, joining time, pay for joining time, age of superannuation and other service conditions shall be in accordance with the regulations approved by the State Government.

CHAPTER VI
MISCELLANEOUS
16. Appointment of Convener, Expert or Agency by the Authority.—To facilitate the discharge of functions under sections 32 and 34 of the Act, the Authority may, with the prior approval of the Government, appoint a Convener, Expert or Agency.
To Conveners, Experts or Agencies,—
(a) a monthly honorarium as determined from time to time by the State Government shall be paid;
(b) they shall not be considered as regular members of the staff class on the establishment of the Authority;
(c) they may be appointed for a period not exceeding one year, which period may be extended on an annual basis;
(d) their service period of appointment may be terminated by the Authority by serving one month's notice.
17. Interpretation.—If any question arises relating to the interpretation of these rules or if no explicit provision has been made in these rules regarding any specific matter, that matter shall be referred to the State Government for decision. The State Government shall make a decision stating reasons within the purview of the Act. The decision of the State Government shall be binding on the Authority.
18. Residuary provisions.—In respect of any matters relating to the terms and conditions of service of the Authority, Chairperson and Members for which no explicit provision has been made in these rules, the Authority shall refer the matter to the State Government for decision, and the decision of the State Government thereon shall be binding on the Chairperson or, as the case may be, the Members.

FORM - II

Form of Oath of Secrecy for the Chairperson/Members of the Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority
I, ........................., having been appointed as the Chairperson/a Member (strike out the portion not applicable) of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority, do solemnly affirm and (or) swear in the name of God that, except as may be required for the due discharge of my duties as Chairperson/Member (strike out the portion not applicable), I will not directly or indirectly communicate or reveal to any person or persons any matter brought under my consideration or known to me.
Date: (Name of Chairperson / Member),
Real Estate Regulatory Authority.

[See rule 10]
Declaration against acquisition of any adverse financial or other interest
I, ........................., having been appointed as the Chairperson/Member (strike out the portion not applicable) of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority, do solemnly affirm and declare that I do not have, nor shall have in future, any financial or other interest of such nature as is likely to affect prejudicially my functioning as the Chairperson/Member (strike out the portion not applicable) of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority.
Date: (Name of Chairperson / Member),
Real Estate Regulatory Authority.
